page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-density server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing a memory allocation of 3.75 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in cryptography, ray tracing, and software compilation. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 577.03 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 247.9 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Single-core performance is moderate, falling into the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests.

This instance is optimized for highly parallelized workloads that benefit from massive multi-core scaling and advanced vector or matrix instructions. It is well-suited for large-scale software compilation, database operations, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based large language model inference, where its AMX capabilities deliver strong prompt processing and text generation speeds. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated compute resources and top-tier memory bandwidth provide a robust platform for consolidating heavy enterprise workloads without the overhead of GPU accelerators.
